To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the integration of ontology modeling, data integration and Web portal design is a promising approach for the creation of data-intensive Web sites (2) the integration of semi-structured data and ontologies is feasible and (3) the integration of ontologies and data-intensive Web sites is possible
the integration of the three approaches mentioned above leads to the creation of a comprehensive system for Web site creation.

the integration of the three different approaches results in a comprehensive solution to the problem of Web site and portal creation, which is more efficient and effective than the current state-of-the-art.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following questions.

the following issues: How to design a Web site in a reusable and flexible way? How to model and integrate data from multiple sources into a single data model? How to use ontologies to model the Web site and its data model? How can the data integration be achieved? What are the benefits of the approach? How to implement the solution?
developing a methodology and system for the creation of reusable Web site specifications and the generation of data-intensive Web sites from these specifications.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
we have shown that it is possible to create a Web site management system that is based on the use of ontological models.
we believe that the OntoWebber system is a significant step towards the vision of the Semantic Web.

we have shown that the combination of ontology technology, semi-structured data modeling and model-driven Web site development can result in a powerful and flexible solution for the creation of reusable Web sites.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have created a system for creating reusable Web site models, which are then transformed into Web pages, which are automatically maintained by the system.
the Semantic Web can benefit from Web portal technology and vice versa.

OntoWebber allows the specification and implementation of Web sites as well as the integration of data from different data sources, and it is the first approach to model and implement Web sites in a way that the model and the implementation are based on ontologies.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the combination of ontologies, data integration technology, and Web site design is very powerful for the creation of data-intensive Web sites, and in particular Web portals.
the combination of ontology technology, semi-structured data and model-driven development is a powerful and promising combination that can be successfully used to create data-intensive Web portals.

the integration of ontology modeling, semi-structured data modeling, and Web site modeling is a promising approach for the development of Web sites and especially for the development of Semantic Web portals.
